summary: PR #59 (release-gem 1.4.1 -> 1.4.2 SHA pin bump) requires no code change. The reported 'FAILING' checks (test (macos-latest, 3.4) and test (macos-latest, 3.3), both 'cancelled') are caused by a GitHub-side macOS arm64 hosted-runner capacity shortage, not by this PR or the repo's CI config: the GitHub Actions job pages for both jobs show zero executed steps and the annotation 'The job was not acquired by Runner of type hosted even after multiple attempts' plus notices that macOS arm64 runners face longer queue times due to capacity constraints, alongside an internal server error. The identical 3-Ruby-version macOS matrix has completed successfully in every prior CI run on this repo over the past several months, so this is a transient external outage, not a structural defect to fix in the workflow. The real, fixable issues on this branch (Ruby 3.2/numo-narray GCC incompatibility on ubuntu-latest, and a lint failure) were already corrected by the pre-existing commit 58478f6 on this branch, which is confirmed green (lint, security, integration, and all other test matrix cells passed in the same run). No workflow edit was made; re-running the two cancelled macOS jobs once GitHub's macOS runner capacity recovers is the correct remediation, not a code change.

verification.rationale: Confirmed via the GitHub Actions REST API and job pages that the two failing checks never acquired a hosted macOS runner (steps: [], runner_id: 0) and were cancelled only after GitHub reported capacity-constraint annotations and an internal server error for macOS arm64 runners, while every other job in the same run (lint, security, integration, and 6 of 8 test matrix cells including macos-latest/3.2) completed successfully.
limitations: Paid cannot re-run GitHub-hosted jobs or confirm GitHub's internal runner capacity has recovered.
No GitHub Status incident was posted for this date, so the capacity shortage is inferred from the job's own annotations rather than an official incident record.
